Span and W. Wagner, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 25 (1996) 1509, DOI 10.1063/1.555991, density uncertain by 0.03–0.05% to 30 MPa and 523 K; https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/fluid.cgi?Action=Data&Wide=on&ID=C124389&Type=SatP&Digits=7&THigh=216.61&TLow=216.6&TInc=0.01&RefState=DEF&TUnit=K&PUnit=MPa&DUnit=mol%2Fl&HUnit=kJ%2Fmol&WUnit=m%2Fs&VisUnit=uPa*s&STUnit=N%2Fm, SHA-256 e276ec7e0bfa52c5fd438baea2655f8699aab160d7f76c4ed37633be70486615, fetched 2026-10-16), 1.17843 g cm⁻³ at the WebBook's molecular weight, 44.0095 (its species page, https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C124389&Units=SI, SHA-256 2c9c9ec9dee087961fa10324e5c26397f4d3bfcfb691af9700b7f16cc5a57e48, fetched 2026-10-16). Phillips measured CO2's Lorentz–Lorenz function at 34 °C and 546.1 nm with a Fabry–Perot etalon up to 0.73692 g cm⁻³: (n² + 2)ρ ÷ (n² − 1) = 6.581(1 + 0.0172ρ²) (p. 236; public domain; the archive.org copy, its text, https://archive.org/download/philtrans01698142/01698142_djvu.txt, SHA-256 f1470244531e81dfcb236cebc31f779990f7ea9b4fc56b533a9b2927e6431529, fetched 2026-10-16, and its page image, https://archive.org/download/philtrans01698142/page/n11_w1300.jpg, SHA-256 a0faa688f4e36a5a94caecfa514737020d77acc832529fb627cd238211d12b69), so the molar refraction is the gas's times c = 1 ÷ (1 + 0.0172ρ²) = 0.976672 here, −0.0072 in n at 546.1 nm, the law extrapolated from his 0.73692 to 1.178 g cm⁻³. His ρ → 0 limit, 44.0095 ÷ 6.581 = 6.687 cm³ mol⁻¹ at 546.1 nm, lies +0.06% from the gas row's 6.683. Bleekrode 1884's saturated liquid at the sodium lines, his air-free tube II (p. 353; public domain; the archive.org copy's page image, https://archive.org/download/paper-doi-10_1098_rspl_1884_0039/page/n14_w1400.jpg, SHA-256 1edc75295d81d2a91e85f92747cc042e12cc9f8a691d89943e4fc9d584970786, fetched 2026-10-16; ±0.005, his error estimate), at the WebBook's densities (https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/fluid.cgi?Action=Data&Wide=on&ID=C124389&Type=SatP&Digits=7&THigh=297.15&TLow=285.65&TInc=0.5&RefState=DEF&TUnit=K&PUnit=MPa&DUnit=mol%2Fl&HUnit=kJ%2Fmol&WUnit=m%2Fs&VisUnit=uPa*s&STUnit=N%2Fm, SHA-256 8b98026a63d71d07318db1307cd1c4cbfd3c6fb265e53eea5a3f1f770c3da7cc, fetched 2026-10-16): 1.199 at 12.5 °C, the file's form less it −0.0023 and the unscaled estimate less it +0.0002; 1.184 at 17.5 °C, the file's form less it +0.0023 and the unscaled estimate less it +0.0045; 1.173 at 24 °C, the file's form less it −0.0042 and the unscaled estimate less it −0.0026; his first table's two sodium values, 1.192 at 15.5 °C (the form less it −0.0013) and 1.186 at 18.5 °C (the form less it −0.0020), are recorded too; his tube I held air, which lowers the index. Near the critical point the form needs no rule of its own: Phillips's law runs smoothly through the near-critical densities, and the errors there are the density's and the scattering's. The sim's carry of this file to another state at a constant Lorentz–Lorenz function misses the form by −0.0024 at 12.5 °C, −0.0025 at 17.5 °C, −0.0025 at 24 °C and −0.0022 at the critical density, 10.6249 mol/l (Span and Wagner's, as the WebBook's page gives it: its fluid page's critical density, https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/fluid.cgi?Action=Load&ID=C124389&Type=SatP&Digits=7&THigh=216.61&TLow=216.6&TInc=0.01&RefState=DEF&TUnit=K&PUnit=MPa&DUnit=mol%2Fl&HUnit=kJ%2Fmol&WUnit=m%2Fs&VisUnit=uPa*s&STUnit=N%2Fm, SHA-256 445c0564eb90a35bfe3ab272d3c02a46d1a3c15e06c3b92176bbdb93918d2c68, fetched 2026-10-16), at 589.3 nm: recorded, not corrected (decision-p14-t49h-gas-index §2.4). n is 1.2862 at 380 nm, 1.27873 at 550 nm, 1.2752 at 780 nm.
